SugarCraft\Flappy

Bird final class

The bird's vertical motion is a SugarSpring Projectile with gravity pulling down at a constant rate. Tapping flap resets the vertical velocity to a fixed upward kick — same trick the original flapioca uses, just expressed as projectile state instead of an ad-hoc accumulator. Mirrors kbrgl/flapioca Model.Cursor (internal/model.go).

Game final class

Flappy-Bird as a SugarCraft Model. The world is width × height cells; the bird sits at column 8 and the world scrolls past it at a fixed cadence. Pipes spawn on the right edge every Game::PIPE_EVERY ticks and slide left one column per tick.

settleOnExit(): GameProcess-boundary settle used by bin/candy-flappy after Program::run() returns. q/Esc already settle inside update() via a batched Cmd; the gap this closes is a signal death (Ctrl+C), where no KeyMsg ever ran and a live qualifying score would be lost. Idempotent: the settledScore stamp means a repeat call after a banking one is a no-op. A failed final save is reported there and then — see the catch — this method never throws and never touches the exit status. Returns the settled model: the banked run with its new-record flag when this call landed a fresh record on disk (flappy-70's ack line reads it), otherwise the unchanged instance.

Pipe final class

One scrolling pipe pair. gapHeight is the number of OPEN rows between the upper and lower sections (m25: it is not a centre marker's symmetric radius). The band is anchored on gapY and, for even heights, tilts one row toward the floor — see collides(). Mirrors the obstacles of kbrgl/flapioca Model.Obstacles (internal/model.go — obst.Location.X--).

MethodSummary

tick(): selfSlide the pipe one column to the left.
collides(int $col, int $row): boolTrue if the bird at (col, row) collides with the pipe. The pipe occupies a single column; collisions happen iff the bird is in that column AND the row is outside the open gap.
isOffScreen(): bool

Renderer final class

Pure view function: takes a Game and returns the framebuffer string. Walks the playfield once, fills every cell, then frames it with a rounded border.

MethodSummary
static render(Game $g): string

TickMsg final class

Frame-tick. Fired every Game::TICK_SECONDS seconds (~30 fps) by the game-tick subscription that Game::subscriptions() declares — a periodic timer the Program owns, re-armed by the event loop itself (there is no fiber; sugar-core runs on a ReactPHP event loop).

SugarCraft\Flappy\Support

Version final class

The version string this tool reports on --version.

MethodSummary
static line(): stringThe --version line: plain text, newline-terminated, produced by no state and no host probe — the flag must answer anywhere.
static current(): stringThe version this process reports: the archive stamp when running from a stamped phar, self::CURRENT everywhere else.
static fromPharMetadata(string $path): ?stringThe version a phar archive at $path was built to carry, or null when it names none (unreadable archive, wrong metadata shape, the dev-build sentinel, or an empty stamp). Every refusal is a null, never an exception — --version must answer on a machine whose phar cannot be opened.
static versionFromMetadata(mixed $metadata): ?stringThe judgement on the stamp itself, split out because the archive-open leg is unreachable from a suite that must not build phars: the release namespace strip, the dev-build refusal, and the wrong-type nulls are a pure function over what getMetadata() answers.
static hostArchive(): stringThe filesystem path of the phar this process was launched from, or '' when it was not launched from one — the two-identity law measured on candy-code's real builds and pinned by the bin autoload guard: inside archive-loaded code Phar::running(false) answers the archive path, while the stub context answers '' and there a '.phar'-suffixed __DIR__ is the enclosing archive.
